title: Yellow Kroeung
description: The lemongrass and turmeric paste that sits under most Khmer cooking. Pounded, never blended, and made in a batch — this yields about a cupful, enough to season two curries.
notes: A food processor will give you something yellow and fragrant, and it will not be kroeung. Blades cut the lemongrass fibre into short splinters; a pestle crushes it open and releases the oil. If you must use a machine, pound the lemongrass by hand first and blitz the rest.

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks
ingredients.note: outer layers stripped, pale core only, sliced as thinly as possible

ingredients.name: galangal
ingredients.note: peeled and sliced across the grain

ingredients.name: turmeric
ingredients.note: the fresh root, peeled; 2 tsp of the dried powder at a push

ingredients.name: dried red chillies
ingredients.note: soaked in warm water and drained

ingredients.name: shrimp paste
ingredients.note: toasted in foil until it smells of the sea

steps.text: Slice the lemongrass stalks as thinly as your knife allows, working only with the pale core.
steps.tip: This is the difference between a smooth paste and one full of splinters. If a slice bends instead of snapping, it belongs in the stock pot.

steps.text: Pound the lemongrass with the salt on its own until it collapses into a wet green pulp.
steps.tip: The salt is the abrasive. Pound the toughest thing first, with nothing soft to cushion it, and the mortar does the work instead of your shoulder.

steps.text: Add the makrut lime leaves and the galangal and keep going until neither is recognisable in the pulp.
Work in the turmeric, then the shallots and the garlic, one at a time and never two together.
steps.tip: The order matters. Anything wet added early turns the mortar into a bowl of soup and the fibres never break down after that.

steps.text: Pound in the dried red chillies and the shrimp paste last if you are using them, then rub a little of the paste between your fingers to check it is smooth.
Pack the kroeung into a jar, press the surface flat, and film it with a thin layer of oil.
steps.tip: A week in the fridge, or freeze it in tablespoon blobs. It darkens as it sits, which is oxidation and not spoilage.
